semantic_inputs: current role-local MANIFEST.json and payload.bin path SHAs

milestone.name: two-identity + config reuse capsule
milestone.revision: The reuse gate scales compositionally: one additional artifact identity adds one repository SHA read and one finite equality/decision layer. In the two-identity test the positive proof used 2 identity reads and 10 check records; changed config, changed manifest identity and changed payload identity each failed closed. No binary semantic read or rebuild was required.

multi_identity_reuse.scope: two already-present Git identities plus declared release flag

linearity.claim: metadata reads scale one-per-bound-path and proof records add constant local checks per added identity; not a runtime benchmark

negative_evidence: Identity gating remains reuse-only and cannot produce a missing artifact.
Even exact manifest+payload Git SHAs do not imply payload behavior.
The release decision does not execute any external release/send/deploy effect.

frontier.action: Use the readable current MANIFEST.json as the source of the expected payload SHA instead of hardcoding it in the checker. Verify manifest path identity, parse payload_path/payload_blob_sha, resolve current payload path SHA and check cross-binding. This tests a proof-carrying manifest pattern that bridges readable metadata to opaque artifact identity without binary byte semantics.
Inject a stale manifest/payload relation in a new role-local probe or as a premise-level negative and require cross-binding failure. Keep actual r145 capsule intact.

Audit standardized content-addressed attestation/manifest schemes for the same subject-digest pattern, but do not claim raw signature verification unless an actually exposed verifier exists with zero optional quota.

exact_next_action: Read the current r145 MANIFEST.json text as an authoritative role-local readable premise, extract payload_path and payload_blob_sha, and compare that declared SHA to the connector-exposed current Git blob SHA at the resolved payload path. Build a finite MANIFEST_BINDING_OK certificate. Negative controls: mutate the manifest-declared SHA and mutate the relative path to an absent/wrong identity; both must fail. Do not use payload bytes, rebuild, cryptographic signature execution or external services.
termination: intermediate Phase-1 checkpoint; global completion false; frontier nonempty
